title: 1812: timber along the South Branch and groves in the wet hollows
items: The South Branch's east bank carries a belt of cottonwood, ash, elm, maple and willow south of the forks, thick by the water and thinning into groves, as Andreas has the South Side timber following the river two or three miles south.
Groves of willow, cottonwood and green ash stand in the low wet ground of the south prairie, and the higher ground stays open grass.
1812 only, and the trails stay clear. Where each grove stands is ours, recorded as a liberty.
